text:
maria: heads-up — seeing intermittent checksum mismatches on overlayfs mounted over /scratch on gnode-eu2-*. 3 nodes stuck in 'provisioning:hold' due to attach failures. kernel logs show unexpected NVMe power-cycle events around 03:14 UTC.

maria: journal snippet:
```
Mar 03 03:14:12 kernel: nvme0: registered pcie dev
Mar 03 03:14:12 kernel: nvme nvme0: I/O device reset failed
Mar 03 03:14:12 kernel: overlayfs: checksum mismatch on lower layer
```

alex: can you paste `iostat -x 1 3` and `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`?

maria: quick outputs (sanitized):
``iostat -x 1 3`
Device    r/s   w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1  0.2   85.3  0.0    512.0    6.0       18.3   0.12   99.5
``
``nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1``
critical_warning: 0
power_cycles: 34 -> 142 (jumped)
media_errors: 0
temperature: 41 C

sai: that power_cycle count jump is suspicious. vendor FW 2.1.7 had a known regression with aggressive power management. any firmware pushes last night? @deploy-bot could you confirm?

deploy-bot: rollout finished: nvme-fw-rollout v2026-03-02-21:10 by infra-release. ID: fw-20260302

jen: if FW correlates, impact is non-trivial — 12 GPU attaches pending in eu-west2, effective capacity down ~6%. fallback plan? DR to dedicated pools will raise cost.

maria: mitigation applied: cordoned offending gnodes, bumped janitor scrub interval from 30m -> 6h to reduce fsync pressure, and set attach policy to prefer healthy-pool fallback for new jobs.

alex: also added temporary scheduler filter: avoid nodes where nvme.power_cycle > 30. I'll open vendor ticket.

sai: escalate to hardware vendor and consider rolling back FW. proposed plan: 02:00 UTC canary rollback (20% of affected hosts), monitor for power_cycle deltas.

jen: ok. capture disk snapshots before rollback? note snapshots cost ~ $0.40/GB — ~250GB per node -> ~$100 per node in snapshot storage; 3 nodes => ~$300. approve?

maria: captured core dumps and nvme logs; uploaded artifacts to /mnt/ops/ephemeral-checksums/1758882134.tar.gz. snapshots pending confirmation.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-224 — ephemeral-nvme-powercycle-checksum-flap. severity set to P1.

alex: action items: 1) vendor ticket w/ logs & FW version, 2) schedule 02:00 UTC canary rollback if vendor recommends, 3) add probe to alert on power_cycle delta > 5 in 1h and auto-cordon.

sai: temp capacity mitigation: enable burst on Dedicated for queued jobs in eu-west2 (billing notif to be sent). jen, please approve budget for burst.

jen: approved up to 3 hours of burst for eu-west2. notify billing and ops.

maria: monitoring note — after cordon + scrub throttle, power_cycle counters stopped increasing on two of three nodes. still watching the third.

alex: I'll implement the probe and the scheduler filter change in next 15m.

oncall-bot: incident severity updated: P1 -> P2 after mitigation.

sai: vendor responded: FW regression acknowledged, rollback recommended. they provided rollback image fw-20251230.

jen: proceed with canary rollback at 02:00 UTC; if canary fails, full rolling rollback with 1-host-at-a-time cadence. ops to estimate expected downtime per host (~5m) and GPU attach ripple.

maria: update ~2h later — power_cycle delta stopped on the remaining node after we cordoned and increased scrub interval. vendor rollback queued for canary. will post results after canary.

alex: added runbook snippet to detect and auto-cordon: `nvmectl probe --delta-threshold 5 --window 3600 && kubectl cordon $NODE` — will PR.

jen: closing P1 -> keep monitoring until post-rollback verification. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
